subheadline: The 24-year-old won every first-place vote for the NL award, weeks after helping Milwaukee win its first World Series.
description: Jacob Misiorowski won the 2026 NL Cy Young unanimously on Nov. 11 after a 1.80 ERA and 252 strikeouts. Why his No. 32 Brewers jersey is one to get now.

body: Jacob Misiorowski is now the best pitcher in the National League by unanimous vote. The Brewers right-hander took all 30 first-place votes for the 2026 NL Cy Young Award, announced on Nov. 11, and became the first unanimous winner in franchise history.
He did it in his first full big league season, at 24, going 16-5 with a major league best 1.80 ERA and 252 strikeouts.
## Why fans are buying in

The numbers go beyond a good year. Misiorowski led the majors in ERA, strikeouts and opponents' batting average, which held at .157. Since 1950, only Sandy Koufax, J.R. Richard and Mike Scott had led the majors in all three. His 0.80 WHIP was the lowest by a pitcher with at least 150 innings since 2000, and he threw 1,115 pitches at 100 mph or faster, the most since pitch tracking began in 2008.

Then came October. Milwaukee beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in the World Series for its first championship, and Misiorowski went 2-0 with a 0.84 ERA in the series, including 5 2/3 scoreless innings in the clinching Game 5. Cy Young ballots were due before the playoffs, so the award covers only his regular season.

He joins Rollie Fingers, Pete Vuckovich and Corbin Burnes as Brewers pitchers who have won the award. In our analysis, a young ace who delivered a title and a historic season in the same year is the kind of player a fan base builds around for a decade. This is our view, not a sales figure.
## The look

Misiorowski wears No. 32. The banner above shows the cream Brewers home jersey, including a version with the 2026 World Series champions patch, a way to mark both the title and the award with one shirt.
## Why this jersey will last

He is 24, a World Series champion and the first unanimous Cy Young winner the Brewers have ever had. subheadline: In his first full season, the right-hander led the American League in ERA and WAR and took all 30 first-place votes.

body: Cam Schlittler went from a late-season call-up to the best pitcher in the American League in about a year. The Yankees right-hander won the 2026 AL Cy Young Award on Nov. 11 with all 30 first-place votes and 210 points, well ahead of Toronto's Dylan Cease at 110.
In 33 starts he went 14-6 with a league-leading 1.95 ERA, 239 strikeouts in 193 2/3 innings and an AL-best 7.0 WAR.
## Why fans are buying in

This was Schlittler's first full season in the majors. He arrived late in 2025, and in 2024 he had been named the Yankees' top minor league pitcher. Even after Gerrit Cole returned midseason, Schlittler was the one New York handed the ball to in Game 1 of the Wild Card round against Boston.

The history adds weight. He is only the 14th American League pitcher to win the award unanimously and the third Yankee, after Ron Guidry in 1978 and Cole in 2023. He is the seventh Yankees pitcher to win it at all, a list that also includes Whitey Ford and Roger Clemens.

In our analysis, a homegrown starter who becomes the ace of the most visible team in baseball is a rare thing, and Yankees fans tend to adopt that kind of player for years. This is our view, not a sales figure.
## The look

Schlittler wears No. 31. The banner above shows the classic white pinstriped Yankees home jersey, the look most fans picture for a New York ace, in men's and women's cuts. It is a design the Yankees have kept largely the same for generations, so it does not date.
## Why this jersey will last

A first full season that ends with a unanimous Cy Young sets a very high bar, and it also makes Schlittler one of the faces of the Yankees' rotation going forward. body: Franz Wagner is carrying Orlando right now. He scored 38 points on 13-of-23 shooting as the Magic beat the Utah Jazz 123-108 on Nov. 11, tying his career high and reaching 30 points for the third game in a row.
Orlando closed the night with an 18-3 run and outscored Utah 38-21 in the fourth quarter.
## Why fans are buying in

Wagner is doing more than scoring. Through the win he was averaging 23.5 points, 6.5 rebounds, 7.9 assists and 1.4 steals, numbers that put the ball in his hands as Orlando's main playmaker. With Paolo Banchero out, the offense now runs through him.

That matters after a stop-start 2025-26 season in which an ankle injury limited him to 34 games. He is 25, the No. 8 pick of the 2021 draft, and still looking for his first All-Star selection, so a hot November is the kind of run that can change how the league sees him.

He also had help. Desmond Bane scored 25 with seven 3-pointers and Anthony Black added 22 points and eight assists as the Magic moved to 4-7, with all four wins coming on the road. In our analysis, a young forward who takes on a bigger role and starts piling up 30-point nights is exactly the player fans start to rally around. This is our view, not a sales figure.
